Welcome
Objective

The purpose of this questionnaire is to collect key business requirements and to define an organization’s future process and solution configurations related to the SciQuest solutions. We hope you will spend time completing this questionnaire to allow for a smooth transition to your Professional Services Implementation team.
This document should be completed and returned with the items below. Please direct any questions to your SciQuest contact.
Item Checklist
Total Supplier Manager (TSM)

The TSM portion of this questionnaire is intended to gather information about how you register and onboard suppliers today, and how you intend to do that process with TSM. The more we can learn about your business processes and requirements, the better we can tailor TSM to meet your needs. Please answer as many of the questions as you can with as much detail as you can provide. Keep in mind that the project team will be reviewing this document with you as part of the beginning of the implementation process.
Supplier Registration & Onboarding
1. Please describe how you register a supplier today.
2. Do you intake cold-calls or by invitation only?
3. Describe the review process for a supplier record after submission.
4. How do you intend this process to change by implementing TSM?

2. For example, describe how you collect accounts payable information (ACH vs. check) or tax information (W9, 1099, State Forms, etc.) for suppliers with whom you want to do business.

Sourcing Director

The Sourcing Director portion of this questionnaire is intended to gather information about your organization’s sourcing activities. It will help the Implementation team understand current processes and begin to think about the design of the application
General Process & Requirements

Sourcing Director allows you to determine which types of events you would like to create. Examples of these are RFI (Request for Information), RFP (Request for Proposal), and RFQ (Request for Quote). Your organization may use these or other names to define your event types.
1. Please the event types that your organization uses below, with a short acronym for each (3 – 7 letters), and if they include the options listed below:
1. Could you briefly describe what tools and processes you currently use to evaluate submissions and make awards?
1. Describe goals in implementing Sourcing Director: How do you hope to improve your processes described above and how will you measure success?

Commodity Code Configuration

In the supplier registration process sourcing director allows your suppliers to select a commodity code which corresponds to products / services that you purchase. When creating a sourcing event you can search for suppliers by commodity code selected in their registration. These commodity codes can be specific codes that your organization uses or a standardized list (NAICS , UNSPSC, etc..)
1. If the above functionality will be used, please provide a list of the commodity codes in the spreadsheet below.
Contract Repository Manager (CRM) & Total Contract Manager (TCM)
This portion of this questionnaire is intended to gather information for the Contract Repository Manager and Total Contract Manager applications.
Visibility
Projects

Contracts are managed through project structures with unique access rights. The flexible design works for a variety of business environments. For example, public or sensitive documents can be set up in separate projects with their own distinct access rights. Or, projects can be divided by business divisions or geographies for easy separation of duties in large organizations.
Users assigned to projects are automatically assigned to contracts within a project to simplify security administration and contract creation.
Projects Example:
1. Please describe any need to limit visibility of contracts to specific users/departments:
Contract Types
The use of a Contract Type determines the extent of content a user will need as part of creating a contract.

Contract types are a key component of the application, since the properties of the contract type are inherited by every contract created from them. A contract type defines the category of contract. It also helps direct the user to the proper Template for Authoring (feature of TCM).
The application supports a wide variety of contract types. Examples include:
1. Revenue based
2. Revenue-based
3. Expenditure-based
4. Non-monetary type agreements
The application also supports:
1. Master/sub-contracts (Parent/Child)
2. Contracts with both buy and sell components
3. Zero dollar value contracts
4. Intellectual property
5. NDA
1. Please list the various Contract Types that your organization uses:
Contract Types Hierarchy example:
Custom & Standard Fields
Custom Fields

In addition to the standard fields (shown in next section), Contract Manager Repository allows your organization to define your own custom fields for capturing data on a contract. Custom Fields can be configured with a wide variety of different response types, including:
1. Text (single line or multiple)
2. Numeric
3. Yes/No
4. Dropdown options (select one)
5. Multiple choice (select one)
6. Multiple select (select many)
7. Date
Conditional Custom Fields

Conditional Custom Fields are also available and can be populated based upon the response of another Custom Field. Please see the example below. Questions can be organized for optimal display for the contract manager, including using pages or groups.
Question: “Are there any non-standard clauses?”
1. No = No action
2. Yes = requires user add detail notes in a text box that is triggered when selecting Yes.
Conditional Custom Field type can be different from the trigger (EG: The response of a Yes/No custom field can generate a new Date, Drop Down, Numeric Text Box, etc. custom field).
Custom Field Placement
Custom Contract Fields can be added to any contract type. As contract types are hierarchical, the inheritance of the custom fields will be followed from parent to child contract types.
Please note that:
1. The layout of the standard fields cannot be changed but can be hidden
2. Custom fields cannot be added to the standard sections/header
Standard Fields

There are pre-defined Standard Fields within Contract Manager Repository. Please review the list below and compare the Standard Fields to the fields that your organization requires. Ask yourself what fields you report out on, what fields your users search on, etc. As mentioned above, Custom Fields can be created for any desired field that is not included in the table below.
1. In the table above, please enter in any custom fields that will be needed for your organization. When filling in this information, follow the guidelines listed below.
2. Identify a logical grouping/category for the new field (Financials, Protections, Contract Request Checklist, General Information, Vendor Information, etc.)
3. Enter the Field Label of the additional field needed
4. Enter the Response Type for the Custom Field (text, numeric, yes/no, etc.)
Templates
A contract template is a structured document consisting boiler plate language with data elements and additional predetermined settings based on a contract type.

1. Is there currently a template approval process in place when new templates or modifications are done? If so, briefly describe this process.

eProcurement

This portion of this questionnaire is intended to gather information about your organization’s sourcing activities. It will help the Implementation team understand current processes and begin to think about the design of the application
General Configuration

1. Is your organization tax exempt on any or all purchases?
1. Please provide an estimate of the number of active contracts with suppliers that will be used in SelectSite.
Project Roles and Responsibilities
1. Are there any key dates where the various resources will not be available for project work? (Holidays, Vacations, Other projects, Year End, Etc.)
1. Do you have any concurrent or near term projects that may impact the implementation of your SciQuest solution?
Accounting Segments
Most organizations require users to assign account values to purchases. The purpose of this section is to determine your organization’s accounting segments that will be used in SelectSite
1. What is the fully qualified account code string used by your general ledger? For example, Company, Division, GL, Department (xxx-xxx-xxxxxxx-xxx).
1. Please list each segment below:

1. Are any of the above segments associated with the other segments? For example, Segment 1 has a specific set of Segment 2 values that apply. In this instance, SciQuest would refer to Segment 1 as the Parent and Segment 2 as the Child. Please identify any parent/child relationships with your accounting elements and if the relationship is one to one (one unique parent to one unique child), one to many (one unique parent to many children), or many to one (many parents to one unique child).
1. Please provide a sample file that contains at least a subset of all values for each field listed above and relationships noted.
Business Units and Departments

Business Units and Departments in SelectSite are used primarily for workflow, reporting and controlling visibility of orders and order history. These can be used for HR hieracrchy (not within the accounting string), where Business Units are the top level and Departments can belong under each Business Unit. Note that these can be renamed (e.g. Business Units can be renamed to Agencies)
1. Briefly explain how Business Units and Departments are used in your organization.
1. Is there a requirement to restrict visibility of orders among departments? For example, will a user associated with department A be able to see orders for department B?
1. Can users be assigned to a single Business Unit and/or Department? Is the information easily available such that it can be included with a user extract?
Suppliers

1. Develop an initial list of top 30 suppliers who can provide an on-line catalog or website for a set of goods that you purchase. Considerations or drivers may be: Spend, transaction volume, go-live departments, contract status, state mandated contracts, etc. We will utilize this list to identify your list of potential go-live catalog suppliers.

1. Have you identified an authentication technology (SAML, LDAP, etc.)?
1. Is the supplier information in your ERP accurate (addresses, order delivery information)?
